BiblicalUsage: Tanchumeth was an Israelite, the father of Seraiah, who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah after the fall of Jerusalem, when the captains of the forces heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor. He is named once in each account, and only as Seraiah's father. The name is also spelled Tanhumeth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the father named only for his son is still worth the record: in the ruin after the fall, the captains gathered to Gedaliah, and Seraiah came, the son of Tanchumeth, and the gathering itself was hope.
